question:
The side of a cube is measured as $12\ \text{cm}$ with a possible error of $0.04\ \text{cm}$. Using differentials, answer the following:

(a) Estimate the maximum error in its calculated volume and find the corresponding percentage error.

(b) Estimate the maximum error in its calculated total surface area and find the corresponding percentage error.

(c) Compare the two percentage errors.

options.A:
(a) Volume error $5.76$ cm$^3$, percentage error $\frac{2}{3}\%$
(b) Surface-area error $17.28$ cm$^2$, percentage error $1\%$
(c) Surface-area percentage error is greater by $\frac{1}{3}\%$
options.B:
(a) Volume error $17.28$ cm$^3$, percentage error $1\%$
(b) Surface-area error $5.76$ cm$^2$, percentage error $\frac{2}{3}\%$
(c) Volume percentage error is greater by $\frac{1}{3}\%$
options.C:
(a) Volume error $17.28$ cm$^3$, percentage error $0.5\%$
(b) Surface-area error $5.76$ cm$^2$, percentage error $1\%$
(c) Surface-area error is twice the volume error
options.D:
(a) Volume error $34.56$ cm$^3$, percentage error $2\%$
(b) Surface-area error $11.52$ cm$^2$, percentage error $\frac{4}{3}\%$
(c) Both percentage errors are equal
